condition_clusters.evidence: Aetna considers adalimumab medically necessary for adult members with rheumatoid arthritis when the adult has previously received a biologic or targeted synthetic drug indicated for moderately to severely active RA within the past 120 days, or when treating moderately to severely active RA and meeting the biomarker and conventional synthetic therapy failure/intolerance/contraindication requirements described in Section II.A.

For members 2 years of age or older, adalimumab is medically necessary for articular juvenile idiopathic arthritis when the member has previously received a biologic or targeted synthetic drug indicated for moderately to severely active articular JIA, or has had inadequate response to methotrexate or another conventional synthetic drug administered at an adequate dose and duration, or has inadequate response to NSAIDs or intra-articular corticosteroids plus risk factors for poor outcome, including high-risk joints or elevated inflammatory markers.

Adalimumab is medically necessary for adult psoriatic arthritis when the member has previously received a biologic or targeted synthetic indicated for active PsA, or when treating active PsA if the member has mild to moderate disease with inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate, leflunomide, or sulfasalazine, or has enthesitis/predominantly axial disease, or has severe disease.

Adalimumab is medically necessary for members 12 years and older with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa who have previously received a biologic, or who have had an inadequate response to at least 90 days of oral antibiotics for HS, or have an intolerance or contraindication to such antibiotics.

Adalimumab is medically necessary for members who have previously received a biologic for pyoderma gangrenosum, or for those with inadequate response to corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy such as cyclosporine or mycophenolate mofetil, or for those with intolerance or contraindication to those therapies.

condition_clusters.condition_label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related inflammatory arthritis (initial therapy)

Continuation is medically necessary for adult members using adalimumab for moderately to severely active RA who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response with at least 20% improvement from baseline in tender joint count, swollen joint count, pain, or disability.

Continuation is medically necessary for members 2 years and older using adalimumab for moderately to severely active articular JIA who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response with improvement in joint counts or functional ability.

Continuation is medically necessary for adult members using adalimumab for psoriatic arthritis who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response with improvement in swollen or tender joints, dactylitis, enthesitis, axial disease, skin or nail involvement, functional status, or CRP.

condition_clusters.evidence: Continuation is medically necessary for members using adalimumab for moderately to severely active Crohn's disease who achieve or maintain remission, or who demonstrate positive clinical response with improvement in abdominal pain, diarrhea, body weight, abdominal mass, hematocrit, mucosal appearance, or disease activity index scores.

Continuation is medically necessary for members using adalimumab for moderately to severely active UC who achieve or maintain remission, or who show improvement in stool frequency, rectal bleeding, urgency, CRP, fecal calprotectin, mucosal appearance, or disease activity scores such as UCEIS or Mayo score.

Continuation is medically necessary for adults using adalimumab for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response as evidenced by reduction in BSA affected or improvement in signs and symptoms such as itching, redness, flaking, scaling, burning, cracking, or pain.

Continuation is medically necessary for members 12 years and older using adalimumab for moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response with reductions in abscess and inflammatory nodule counts, new sinus tract formation and scarring, lesion frequency, pain, suppuration, relapse frequency, quality of life, or disease severity assessment scores.

Continuation is medically necessary for members 2 years and older using adalimumab for non-infectious intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis who achieve or maintain a positive clinical response with reduced flare frequency, stable or improved anterior chamber cell grade, vitreous haze, visual acuity, glucocorticoid requirements, or absence of new inflammatory retinal lesions.
